repo.description:
A subscriber to a `LIVE SELECT` query could read a field that field-level `SELECT` permissions should have hidden from them, by projecting it out of the `$after` or `$before` event parameter instead of selecting the field by name.

A `LIVE SELECT` delivers a per-subscriber document that has field-level `PERMISSIONS FOR select` applied, so a field the subscriber may not read is cut from the notification payload. The `$value`, `$before`, and `$after` parameters, however, were bound to the unreduced record. A subscriber authorised for the table but not for a field could root a projection at one of those parameters and copy the restricted value straight into the notification:

```surql
LIVE SELECT $after.hidden AS leaked FROM test;
```

`$after` carried the new record on `CREATE` and the post-update record on `UPDATE`; `$before` carried the pre-delete record on `DELETE`. The alias placed the value under a name the payload's field filter did not treat as the restricted field, so it survived into the result. The table's own `SELECT` permission was still enforced, so the subscriber only received records they were already entitled to see - the disclosure was confined to fields within those records.

A related path, testing the restricted field in the `WHERE` clause and observing whether a notification arrives, is covered by [GHSA-jm88-9wvx-6h4q](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/security/advisories/GHSA-jm88-9wvx-6h4q). The same change in 3.3.0 fixes both.

### Impact

Only databases that use field-level `SELECT` permissions - `DEFINE FIELD ... PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE`, or a restricting `WHERE` - to hide a field from users who can otherwise read the table are affected. This is a confidentiality issue at the field-permission boundary.

What an attacker **can** do:

- With permission to run a `LIVE SELECT` on a table (a record user is enough) but no permission to read a particular field, receive that field's value in notifications by projecting it out of `$before` / `$after`, for every record the subscription already delivers, across `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE`.
- Recover the exact stored value, not merely its presence.

What it **can't** do:

- Reach records the subscription is not already entitled to. This issue does not bypass table-level permissions, and exposes nothing across tables, namespaces, or databases.
- Modify data - this is read-only disclosure.
- Escape field-level scope: only fields on the subscribed table's own records are exposed. System users (root, namespace or database users) are unaffected, as they may already read every field.

### Patches

`LIVE SELECT` now binds `$value`, `$before`, and `$after` to the same per-subscriber reduced views used for the notification payload, so a projection rooted at those parameters can no longer read a field the subscriber may not select. Both the pre- and post-mutation images are reduced, so `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` are all covered, in full-document and `DIFF` mode alike.

- Versions 3.3.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### Workarounds

Users unable to patch should consider the following workarounds:

- Do not rely on field-level `SELECT` permissions to hide values on a table that untrusted users can subscribe to; keep sensitive fields in a separate table or database those users cannot read at all, or restrict at the table level.
- Deny live and arbitrary queries to untrusted principal classes with `--deny-arbitrary-query` (env `SURREAL_CAPS_DENY_ARBITRARY_QUERY`), for example for `guest` and `record`, which also blocks the `LIVE` RPC for those classes.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - LIVE SELECT](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/live)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE FIELD](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/field)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE TABLE … PERMISSIONS](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/table)
- `fix(doc): bind LIVE $value/$after/$before to reduced views` (included in SurrealDB 3.3.0)

### Acknowledgements

Thank you to [arbor-s](https://github.com/arbor-s) for reporting this issue.
repo.summary: Field-level SELECT permissions bypassed in LIVE query projections via `$before` / `$after`
